Appearance
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This list details all Premier League managers since the league began in 1992. For current managers only, see List of current Premier League and English Football League managers.

The Premier League is the top tier of professional football in England. The league was formed in 1992 as a replacement for the original Football League First Division. To date, there have been 328 managers in charge of the 51 clubs which have played in the Premier League. 286 of those are permanent appointments, and 123 of them in a caretaker/interim capacity.

Arsène Wenger holds the record for most games managed in the Premier League with 828, all with Arsenal, which he managed between 1996 and 2018.[1] Alex Ferguson won the most games, with 528 wins during his time as manager of Manchester United.[2] Sam Allardyce has managed the most teams in the Premier League, having taken charge of nine different clubs: Bolton Wanderers, Newcastle United, Blackburn Rovers, West Ham United, Sunderland, Crystal Palace, Everton, West Bromwich Albion and Leeds United.[3] The season with the highest number of managers was the 2022–23 season, with 39 managers.[4]

Thirteen managers have won the Premier League since the competition's inception in 1992.[2] The most successful manager is Ferguson, who won 13 titles – more than twice as many as any other manager – with Manchester United between 1993 and 2013.[5] He's followed by Pep Guardiola, who won six titles between 2018 and 2024, followed by Wenger and Jose Mourinho with three each, as managers of Arsenal and Chelsea respectively. Mourinho is the youngest manager to win the Premier League, he was 42 years and 94 days old when he led Chelsea to the title in 2005.[6] Mikel Arteta is the only Premier League manager to win a title with the club he previously played for as a player.[7]

Many of the managers listed below served as caretaker managers in the period between a managerial departure and appointment. Several of these, however, went on to secure a permanent managerial post.

Managers

[edit]

The list of managers includes everyone who has managed clubs while they were in the Premier League, whether in a permanent or temporary role. Caretaker managers are listed only when they managed the team for at least one match in that period.

The dates of appointment and departure may fall outside the club's period in the Premier League, for example, Ron Atkinson was appointed as Aston Villa manager in 1991 (before the Premier League was formed in 1992) and remained in his position through the Premier League's establishment. Similarly, Wolverhampton Wanderers' first spell in the Premier League lasted for only one season (2003–04) but manager Dave Jones remained in his position until November 2004.
